SGLang: Reachable Assertion via  lora_path  in LoRAManager enables remote Denial of Dervice

Aliases: CVE-2026-10300

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P

A security vulnerability has been detected in SGLang 0.5.10.post1. Impacted is an unknown function of the file python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_manager.py of the component Inference HTTP Endpoint. Such manipulation of the argument lora_path leads to reachable assertion. The attack can be launched remotely. A high complexity level is associated with this attack. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-8f95-v3jq-cj86: pymonocypher: Potential heap buffer overflow on nb_blocks in argon2i_32 when provided buffer is too small
entry.content:
pymonocypher: Potential heap buffer overflow on nb_blocks in argon2i_32 when provided buffer is too small

Aliases: CVE-2026-53720

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • pymonocypher — fixed in 4.0.2.8

### Impact The argon2i_32 implementation does not check the nb_blocks size. If the caller does not provide a sufficiently large buffer based on the API contract, then argon2i_32 will write past the end of the buffer and possibly corrupt the heap. ### Patches Fixed in 4.0.2.8, which now verifies that nb_blocks is large enough. See [90ff5b1](https://github.com/jetperch/pymonocypher/commit/90ff5b13b13b5673c372e188f482d8c172e6ab86). ### Workarounds Provide a correctly sized nb_blocks buffer. pymonocypher thanks Haris (hextheshadow) for the vulnerability report, details, and recommended fix.

Before apache-airflow 3.3.0, a user authorized to read one Dag could disclose the source of other Dags co-located in the same source file. `GET /api/v2/dagSources/{dag_id}` — and the equivalent Dag-source view in the UI — returned the entire source file without redacting Dags the caller was not authorized to read, bypassing per-DAG read authorization. Deployments that co-locate multiple Dags in a single file and rely on per-DAG access control to limit source visibility are affected; single-Dag-per-file deployments are not. Upgrade to apache-airflow 3.3.0 or later.

Affected:

  • apache-airflow — fixed in 3.3.0

A bug in `BaseSerialization.deserialize()` allowed unrestricted `import_string()` of attacker-controlled class paths when the Scheduler / API Server loaded a serialized DAG: a DAG author could embed a malicious trigger into a DAG to gain remote code execution on the API Server / Scheduler process, crossing the Airflow security boundary that DAG-author code must never execute in those processes. Users are advised to upgrade to `apache-airflow` 3.3.0 or later. As a defense-in-depth mitigation, deployments where DAG-author trust is limited can restrict the `[core] allowed_deserialization_classes` config to a narrow allowlist.

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-2085: In nltk/nltk versions 3.9.3 and earlier, five Stanford interface classes (StanfordPOSTagger, StanfordNERTagger, Stanford
entry.content:
Aliases: CVE-2026-12252

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • nltk — fixed in 3.9.4

In nltk/nltk versions 3.9.3 and earlier, five Stanford interface classes (StanfordPOSTagger, StanfordNERTagger, StanfordParser, StanfordDependencyParser, and StanfordNeuralDependencyParser) are vulnerable to untrusted JAR code execution. These classes accept user-controllable JAR paths and execute them via the `java()` function, which invokes `subprocess.Popen()` without integrity verification. This vulnerability is identical to CVE-2026-0848, which was fixed for StanfordSegmenter by adding SHA256 verification. However, the fix was not applied to these additional classes, leaving them susceptible to arbitrary code execution when loading untrusted JAR files.

Aliases: BIT-airflow-2026-49298, CVE-2026-49298

Affected:

  • apache-airflow-core — fixed in 3.2.2

A bug in Apache Airflow's KubernetesExecutor caused JWT tokens used by worker pods to authenticate against the Execution API to be passed to the worker container as command-line arguments visible in the pod spec.
